claim_judgments.rationale: The claim accurately reflects the requirement in 29 CFR 825.303(a) that when the approximate timing of the need for leave is not foreseeable, an employee must give notice to the employer as soon as practicable under the facts and circumstances.

The claim faithfully captures the advisory standard in 29 CFR 825.303(a) that it generally should be practicable to give notice of unforeseeable leave within the timeframe prescribed by customary employer notice requirements.
The claim correctly reflects the permission and condition allowing notice to be provided by a spokesperson when the employee is unable to do so personally.
The claim accurately reproduces the regulatory example and exemption regarding an employee taking a child experiencing a severe asthma attack to the emergency room.
The claim accurately conveys the contrasting illustrative scenario in 29 CFR 825.303(a) where prompt notice is expected following an at-home asthma attack treated with an inhaler and rest.
The claim accurately represents the baseline duty in 29 CFR 825.303(b) requiring employees to provide sufficient information for the employer to determine if FMLA applies.
The claim details the descriptive examples of information that may constitute sufficient notice depending on the circumstances.
The claim correctly reflects the exemption in 29 CFR 825.303(b) establishing that first-time leave seekers need not explicitly mention or assert rights under the FMLA.

The claim correctly states the requirement for an employee seeking leave for a previously designated qualifying reason to specifically reference either the qualifying reason or the need for FMLA leave.
The claim correctly states that calling in sick without more information is insufficient to trigger employer statutory obligations under 29 CFR 825.303(b).
The claim accurately captures the expectation that employers obtain additional required leave information through informal means.
The claim accurately states the employee's affirmative duty to respond to employer questions designed to determine whether leave is FMLA-qualifying.
The claim properly reflects the conditional consequence that failure to answer reasonable employer inquiries can result in denial of FMLA protection if coverage cannot be determined.

The claim faithfully conveys the general rule of 29 CFR 825.303(c) mandating compliance with usual and customary notice and procedural requirements absent unusual circumstances when leave is unforeseeable.

The claim extracts an example from 29 CFR 825.303(c) as an unconstrained permission, omitting the governing context that it is an illustrative example of an employer's usual and customary procedural requirements for requesting unforeseeable leave. The scope is overbroad as an empty scope_text admits general unconditioned call-in rules.
The claim accurately captures the emergency medical treatment exemption suspending the call-in procedure until condition stabilization and telephone access.
The claim accurately conveys that advance written notice under internal employer rules may not be required in emergency leave situations involving FMLA.
The claim accurately states the consequence that FMLA-protected leave may be delayed or denied if an employee fails to comply with usual procedural requirements without unusual circumstances.

unit_judgments.rationale: Claim C0000 fully and accurately represents the requirement to provide notice as soon as practicable when leave timing is not foreseeable.

Claim C0003 accurately preserves the emergency room asthma attack illustration and its exemption from reporting during treatment.
Claim C0004 faithfully reflects the expectation of prompt notice following at-home treatment and rest for an asthma attack.
Claim C0005 fully captures the obligation to provide sufficient information to determine FMLA applicability.
Claim C0006 retains the complete set of descriptive categories of sufficient information.
Claim C0007 accurately covers the first-time notice exemption from mentioning FMLA rights.
Claim C0008 accurately captures the requirement to specifically reference the qualifying reason or need for FMLA leave on subsequent requests.
Claim C0009 accurately covers the rule that calling in sick without additional information is insufficient notice.
Claim C0010 preserves the principle that employers are expected to gather additional details informally.
Claim C0011 preserves the employee duty to respond to employer questions assessing FMLA qualification.
Claim C0012 covers the consequence of potential denial of protection when inquiries go unanswered.
Claim C0013 fully covers the mandate to comply with usual notice procedures absent unusual circumstances.

Claim C0014 has summary and scope errors because it detaches the illustrative permission from its governing context as an example of customary notice and procedural requirements for requesting unforeseeable leave.
Claim C0015 accurately conveys the emergency medical treatment exemption from call-in procedures until stabilization and phone access.
Claim C0016 conveys the exemption regarding internal written advance notice requirements during emergencies.
Claim C0017 covers the delay or denial consequence for failure to adhere to usual procedures without unusual circumstances.
